title: Phase 0a operational missing-positive-control review
principle: A retained operational incident can be documented from its bounded counterexample without inventing a second observation. A successful contrast matters when it tests an asserted route contract or distinguishes the failure mechanism; frozen test assertions are cited as source evidence, not claimed as fresh runs.

evidence.supports: numeric commit raises raw TypeError
current initialized metadata with string implementation identity loads and preserves that identity
valid historical string implementation identity validates and is preserved

rows.assessment: Valid string metadata has a frozen successful path. The numeric-field diagnostic itself is retained. A new valid-string execution would not change the candidate claim.
rows.prior_positive_request: Valid string source_commit validates; malformed numeric value returns a structured refusal.

evidence.supports: string integral passes exported schema but native shape refuses
a typed Boolean integral claim participates in a native graph check
retained harness exercised only the string mismatch across both validators

rows.assessment: The mismatch is complete for incident documentation. No retained control applies the same typed-Boolean claim to both exported schema and native validator. The native graph assertion is a partial shared control.

minimum_offline_control.when: only if parent wants an admitted two-sided validator route
minimum_offline_control.vector: Use the same minimal claim event as the retained string control, replacing integral with JSON boolean false; call the exported event schema and native validate_native_event once each offline. Record both outcomes; do not alter a graph.

rows.prior_positive_request: Boolean integral native/exported acceptance and string integral refusal agree.

evidence.supports: same sparse inference retraction passes native shape and fails exported schema
sparse inference retraction folds successfully under native format

rows.assessment: The current two-validator contrast is the incident. There cannot be a successful same-input agreement for this sparse tombstone under the present exported schema. A repair test depends on whether the schema is a complete native contract or a narrower authoring contract.
rows.decision_needed: Choose whether the exported schema must admit native sparse retractions or explicitly remain a narrower authoring schema before requiring an agreement control.
rows.prior_positive_request: Sparse tombstone authoring/export and native shape agree after intended schema policy is stated.

evidence.supports: valid BASE model renders compact handoff
valid ALGEBRAIC_CLOSURE model renders the same compact handoff

rows.assessment: Each side is a successful handoff rendering. The point-scope values differ while rendered text matches. A third positive case adds no mechanism distinction.
rows.prior_positive_request: Q BASE and Q ALGEBRAIC_CLOSURE compact handoffs identify their different point universes.

evidence.supports: injected post-check source change creates archive with mismatched digest
clean synthetic release materializes files and SHA256SUMS
source change after planning but before materialization refuses

rows.assessment: The frozen success and earlier-change refusal cover the ordinary path; the retained injection isolates the later check-to-copy window. Exact archive-byte equality is not separately asserted in the success test, so do not describe that test as a proof of the failing window.
rows.prior_positive_request: Unchanged source copy matches manifest digest; injected source change refuses or rebinds archived digest.

evidence.supports: emit-review overwrites protected manifest input
emit-review overwrites protected receipt input
emit-review to separate review.json succeeds and output matches derived receipt

rows.assessment: The separate-path CLI success is a genuine shared operational control. That frozen test does not record before/after hashes of bound inputs; the overwrite incident is supported by the retained controls themselves.
rows.prior_positive_request: Review emission to a separate path succeeds and bound inputs retain their hashes.

evidence.supports: source reserved-name collision returns success but copied source payload is overwritten
ordinary export without the reserved-name collision is byte exact and validates READY

rows.assessment: The no-collision frozen test supplies the requested successful export contrast. READY here is structural retention, not native graph authority.
rows.prior_positive_request: No reserved source name exports unchanged; collision refuses before output mutation.

evidence.supports: duplicate receipt open list gives receipt count 2 and aggregate unique count 1
single unique open item builds with aggregate open_items [A]
a mismatching receipt open_items list is refused

rows.assessment: The unique-item success is already represented in frozen tests; duplicate-list mismatch is retained. No new control is needed for the incident.
rows.prior_positive_request: Unique open_items maintains matching per-receipt and aggregate counts.

evidence.supports: terminal-newline stable ID is accepted
bare stable ID A participates in a successful frontier build

rows.assessment: Bare A has a frozen successful build, and the retained control records acceptance of A with a terminal newline. A separate direct bare-ID call is unnecessary for incident documentation.
rows.prior_positive_request: Valid stable ID accepted; terminal newline rejected.

evidence.supports: structural intake marks unloadable synthetic graph READY
native load raises GraphError and no report is written
ordinary export validates READY, but its synthetic header does not establish native load or reporter success

rows.assessment: The READY-versus-native-load distinction is fully documented. No cited retained control demonstrates that a valid native graph produces this reporter output. The candidate reason also asks for a per-campaign load-error report, which is a reporting contract choice.

minimum_offline_control.when: if parent keeps a per-campaign report guarantee in the candidate contract
minimum_offline_control.vector: In an isolated offline reporter root, provide one native-loadable graph and the existing malformed kernel_epoch-null campaign; invoke the reporter once and record the valid campaign report, malformed campaign error entry, output file, and overall status. No corpus admission.

rows.decision_needed: Decide whether the contract requires a per-campaign error report after native load refusal, or only refuses to equate structural READY with native report readiness.
rows.prior_positive_request: Valid native graph produces a report; malformed graph yields a per-campaign load error.

evidence.supports: direct injected mutable abort_reason changes artifact fingerprint after construction
artifact with native-shape null abort_reason has stable fingerprint and round-trips
injected normal backend execution snapshots artifact fields and fingerprints

rows.assessment: Stable null abort_reason is covered by a frozen successful artifact path. The mutable-object case is limited to the direct injected adapter; no persisted-object bypass is claimed.
rows.prior_positive_request: Native string/null abort_reason remains stable; direct mutable object is copied/refused.

evidence.supports: the same retained record explicitly has ordinary=true and newline=true for valid_fingerprint

rows.assessment: This row was marked not_retained only because the positive result is co-located with the negative result. Bare 64-hex acceptance is already recorded exactly.
rows.prior_positive_request: Valid 64-hex digest accepted and trailing newline rejected.

evidence.supports: parsed x with caller [1] persists caller [1] in model declaration
matching caller [x] and parsed x persists [x]
changed caller [1] with same parsed x persists [1]

rows.assessment: The previously accepted generator contrast supplies the exact matching positive side. It remains injected-runner metadata persistence, not a proof or CAS truth verdict.
rows.decision_needed: For repair or checker admission, choose whether mismatch must refuse or may persist with explicit caller-versus-output provenance; the current candidate can refuse the stronger parsed-output-origin claim without choosing.
rows.prior_positive_request: Matching caller/output generators bind declaration; mismatch refuses or records explicit provenance difference.

evidence.supports: array baseline raises raw AttributeError
array hook payload raises raw AttributeError
after replacing baseline with object, valid object hook payload reaches normal blocking path
harness replaces baseline with {}, then sends object payload through H.main and records blocking exit

rows.assessment: The same retained harness contains the successful object-shape parsing side, although it is embedded in the malformed-graph block control. The raw array exceptions show the structured-response gap. Host handling after an uncaught hook exception was not tested.
rows.decision_needed: Decide whether candidate wording includes next host event survival. That would require a separate host-protocol observation; the current direct-call evidence supports only the structured-response shape defect.
rows.prior_positive_request: Valid object payloads continue processing; array payloads return structured refusal and next event survives.

evidence.supports: two distinct decoder errors give distinct evaluate messages, while second hook message says unchanged and blocking remains true

rows.assessment: The two-error retained pair is the relevant contrast and keeps the blocking exit. A same-error repetition would document intended suppression but is not needed to establish that different causes are hidden.
rows.prior_positive_request: Same graph error reports unchanged; different decoder errors report changed while exit remains blocking.

decisions_for_parent.question: Is exported event schema complete for native sparse retractions or intentionally narrower authoring guidance?
Does the reporter contract require a per-campaign error record on native load refusal, or only refusal to promote structural READY?
If repairing generator provenance, should mismatch refuse or persist with explicitly distinct caller/output provenance?
Should the candidate promise host next-event survival, or only a structured direct-hook refusal?

unrun_finite_controls: GP-X372 typed-Boolean same-event validator pair if exact route admitted
GP-X389 valid native graph plus malformed campaign reporter pair if per-campaign report contract selected
limits: Frozen test assertions were inspected but not re-run; they are not fresh oracle verdicts.
No live CAS, campaign contents, corpus routing, replay, decisions, trackers, or candidate files were changed.
